records.subject: Difference in total electron energy between two contacting metals
records.object: Peltier coefficient Π = ε0 T ln(1 + T/Θv)
records.quote: Thermodynamic consideration of thermoelectricity in metals was applied to the Peltier effect, like it was done recently for the Seebeck effect.
context_quotes: The Peltier coefficient was derived from the difference in the total energy of electrons in two metals in contact: Pi=epsilon(0)Tln(1+T/Theta(v)), where epsilon(0) is the 'universal' sensitivity of thermocouples and theta(V) is the characteristic temperature of a particular thermocouple.
modality_evidence: Thermodynamic consideration of thermoelectricity in metals was applied to the Peltier effect, like it was done recently for the Seebeck effect.
